job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

passage: Dear Diary, today in Geography class, we learned fascinating facts about our oceans. I used to think that waves carried water all the way from the middle of the sea to the beach, but our teacher explained that waves only move the energy through the water, while the water particles themselves move in small circles. We also discussed why the ocean is salty. It is not because of decaying sea creatures, but because rivers carry dissolved salts from rocks on land into the sea over millions of years. I was surprised to learn that the water cycle is a continuous process where water evaporates from the surface, condenses into clouds, and falls as rain; the clouds do not create new water, they only store and release what has evaporated. Finally, we looked at tides. I learned that tides are the rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water caused primarily by the gravitational pull of the moon, not by the sun pushing the water around. It is amazing how the Earth's water is constantly moving and changing form, yet the total amount of water on our planet remains the same throughout history. Understanding these natural processes makes me appreciate our blue planet so much more. I cannot wait to learn more about ocean currents tomorrow!

items.evidence: I used to think that waves carried water all the way from the middle of the sea to the beach, but our teacher explained that waves only move the energy through the water, while the water particles themselves move in small circles.
items.q: A cork floats far out at sea as waves pass. What does the cork do?
options: It moves in small circles and stays nearby
It is carried straight to the beach
It sinks once the first wave arrives
It moves only when the moon pulls it
items.explain: Waves move energy, not water; the water particles, and the cork, only move in small circles.

wrong.why: thinks waves carry water to the shore
thinks a passing wave pulls floating things under

items.evidence: It is not because of decaying sea creatures, but because rivers carry dissolved salts from rocks on land into the sea over millions of years.
items.q: Why does the sea have much more salt than the river water flowing into it?
options: Salts from land have gathered in it for ages
Dead sea animals dissolve into it each year
Rivers pour in new salty water every day
Its water is salty only near the shore
items.explain: Rivers carry dissolved salts from rocks into the sea over millions of years, so salts build up there.

wrong.why: thinks dissolved sea creatures make it salty
thinks river water is as salty as the sea
thinks salt varies only by distance from land

items.evidence: the clouds do not create new water, they only store and release what has evaporated.
items.q: A heavy rain falls from dark clouds. Where did that rainwater come from?
options: Water that earlier rose from the surface
Water the clouds made from the air
Water that was always kept inside the sun
Water newly formed when the clouds cooled
items.explain: Clouds only store and release water that has evaporated from the surface; they do not make new water.

wrong.why: links the water source to the sun
thinks new water forms by a temperature change

items.evidence: I learned that tides are the rhythmic rise and fall of ocean water caused primarily by the gravitational pull of the moon, not by the sun pushing the water around.
items.q: The sea level at a beach rises and falls twice a day. What mainly causes this?
options: The pull of the moon on the water
The push of the sun on the water
The waves moving water in from far out
The rivers adding salty water each day
items.explain: Tides are caused mainly by the moon's gravitational pull, not by the sun pushing the water.

wrong.why: thinks the sun pushes the water
thinks waves carry water to the shore
picks a nearby detail about rivers

items.evidence: It is amazing how the Earth's water is constantly moving and changing form, yet the total amount of water on our planet remains the same throughout history.
items.q: Farmers use lots of water to grow crops. What happens to the Earth's total water?
options: It stays the same as water keeps cycling
It slowly falls as crops absorb the water
It rises as new water forms in clouds
It falls until the oceans become salty
items.explain: Water keeps moving and changing form, so the total amount on Earth stays the same.

wrong.why: thinks used water is gone forever
mixes up water use with salinity
